To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the theory of orthogonal decomposition of genetic variance can be completed with linkage disequilibria and epistasis; (2) the theory of decomposition of the genetic variance can be used to understand the dynamics of genetic incompatibilities and epistasis under linkage disequilibrium; (3) the theory of genetic variance decomposition can be applied to understand the dynamics and evolution of genetic incompatibility and epistasis.

(i) the classical genetic variance decomposition theory can be extended to the case of LD, (ii) the theory of variance decomposition under LD has a number of novel properties, and (iii) the theory can be applied to the analysis of evolutionary scenarios involving incompatibilities and epistasis.

the classical theory of genetic variance decomposition can be extended to include the effects of linkage disequilibrium and that the theory thus extended provides a novel framework to study the evolution of Bateson-Dobbzhansky-Muller incompatibilities and the evolution of genetic robustness to sign epistasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of genetic systems under LD, and in particular with the analysis of the genetic variance decomposition of traits under epistasis and LD.
the study of genetic variance decomposition for traits with epistasis in a population under linkage disequilibrium.
developing a theory of genetic variance decomposition under linkage disequilibrium and epistasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LD and epistasis do not preclude the use of variance decomposition, but rather they make it more complex and interesting.
, although the theory of genetic variance decomposition under LD is complex, it can be implemented in practice.

, although LD is a complex phenomenon that may lead to unexpected and counterintuitive results, the orthogonal decomposition of the genetic variance is a well-established and robust methodology that is still applicable to epistatic traits with LD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to perform variance decomposition in a system under epistasis and LD, which is a long-awaited goal in the quantitative genetics field.
the genetic variance components are not independent, and their interplay with LD may lead to novel properties that are not present in systems with linkage equilibrium.

, in the presence of epistasis and LD, the genetic variance decomposition can be performed by the same methods used under linkage equilibrium, provided that we consider that the epistatic variance is partitioned into two components: the one due to epistasis and the other due to linkage disequilibrium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory of orthogonal genetic variances decomposition is a powerful tool to understand the evolutionary dynamics of genetic systems under LD and to develop novel methods for quantitative genetics.
LD is not an obstacle to variance decomposition, but rather a new source of complexity to be exploited.
, with the appropriate tools, the analysis of epistasis under LD is possible.
